_about: Intent registry for scripts/ask.py - the 'ask anything' layer.
This is DATA, not code. Adding a question the tool understands means
adding an entry here; the router never changes. That is deliberate:
the set of answerable questions is reviewable in one file, and it is
obvious what the tool can and cannot do without reading Python.
Matching is keyword-based and deliberately dumb. It cannot invent SQL,
so it cannot produce a number that nobody defined. When it does not
recognise a question it says so and lists what it does know, rather
than guessing. See DECISIONS.md for why that trade was chosen over an
LLM writing SQL against the schema.
Fields:
match     - all_of: every term must appear (or any synonym in a group)
any_of: at least one term must appear
query     - the library file to run. NOT written here; the SQL lives
in the library and is shared with human users.
kpi       - catalogue IDs this answers, for the citation line
period    - which parameter names take the resolved date window
blocked   - if present, the question is answerable-sounding but NOT
answerable from these feeds. Returns the documented
reason plus a runnable proof, never a number.

intents.label: Units sold, converted to eaches
intents.caveat: Coverage is ~49.6% of lines - half the history predates the schema change and carries no unit of measure. The query reports its own coverage.

intents.caveat: Mixes eaches and cases - this is NOT a physical volume. Ask for eaches if you need real units.

intents.caveat: The published report cannot be reconciled to - it is not derived from the POS feed at all. This query proves that and sizes the gap.

intents.label: Order value by source system, and comparability
Cold chain excursion rate by month
intents.caveat: Reported at READING grain, 7.19%. A vehicle-day rollup gives 75.07% - the grain is most of the answer. 'Trips' are not defined anywhere in the feed.

intents.label: Which days are missing data, in any feed

reason: The WMS feed contains no stitchable per-item journey. order_number,
sku_code, batch_id, pallet_id and warehouse_code are each drawn
independently per scan row, so nothing ties one item's six handling
stages together.
Verified three ways: stitching RECEIVE->DISPATCH by order_number gives a
NEGATIVE duration for 50.13% of eligible orders - a coin flip, not a
data-quality tail. The same ~50% negative rate holds keying by batch_id
(49.91%) and pallet_id (49.81%), ruling out a wrong join key. And among
the positive-duration half, median implied cycle time is ~155 days.
To unblock: a handling-unit identifier that persists across scan stages.

intents.label: Cold chain excursion rate by carrier

reason: There is no carrier identifier on the telemetry feed, or on any other
raw feed. carrier_master.csv is orphaned reference data - carrier_id is
written once, into that CSV, and referenced nowhere else in the dataset.
dim_carrier is built and conformed, but joins to nothing.
route_code cannot substitute: it is re-randomised on every individual
reading. All 340 vehicles see readings against all 260 route codes and
all 8 warehouses, so it is not an assignment despite what the feed
contract claims.
The BY MONTH half of this question IS answerable - ask for excursion
rate by month. To unblock the carrier split: a vehicle-to-carrier
assignment feed.
The outlet master's versioned attributes are not change history. Six of
nine attributes - channel, outlet_format, city, route_code,
credit_limit, credit_terms_days - are independently re-randomised on
every CDC update, confirmed in the generator.
Answering from dim_outlet.channel would report that the large majority
of outlets 'changed channel'. That is noise presented as a finding, and
it is the kind of number that ends up in a board pack. OUT001011 cycles
GT -> MT -> ECOM -> GT -> MT -> GT -> ECOM and five different cities
across 12 versions, with no pattern.
Only warehouse_code, gst_number and outlet_name are genuinely stable.
To unblock: a source that emits change events only on genuine change.

intents.label: Order net value, order discount, order tax

reason: On the sales_order_header feed, discount_amount and tax_amount are
drawn as free-standing uniforms with no reference to order_value_gross.
Measured on the built fact: corr(gross, discount) = 0.0020,
corr(gross, tax) = 0.0027, and the implied tax rate spans 0.04% to
2552% where a real GST rate would cluster tightly.
Because discount is unbounded relative to gross, 1,743 orders (0.54%)
compute to a NEGATIVE net value - at a near-identical rate in all three
source systems, which rules out the freight correction as the cause.
Use order value GROSS instead - ask for order value by source system.
Note the POS feed is different: there, discount and tax ARE derived from
the line value, so net sales is sound. Ask for a sales summary.

intents.label: Proportion of trips that breached temperature

reason: Nothing in the telemetry feed demarcates a trip. There is no trip
identifier, no ignition or door-cycle boundary that closes a journey,
and no dispatch event to anchor one. The only genuinely stable identity
on the feed is device_id -> vehicle_registration (verified 1:1).
Any trip definition would therefore be invented in the pipeline, and
the choice would drive the headline number: reading grain gives 7.19%,
a naive vehicle-day rollup gives 75.07%. That is why the fact is left
at reading grain deliberately.
Ask for excursion rate by month for the defensible version. To unblock:
a trip or shipment feed, then agree the definition with Operations
BEFORE publishing - this is the number most likely to be misquoted.
